title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from this page and its neighbours. L is a totally ordered set, a model 'line'. M is the set of 'multiplicités', the elementary strata of L: points P_t (t∈L) and open segments S_{a,b} (a<b). δ assigns to a stratum its set of 'endpoints' (δP_t={t}, δS_{a,b}={a,b}). A 'figure' is a finite set of mutually compatible multiplicités. Drap(L) is the set of finite chains of L; since L is totally ordered, these are simply its finite subsets.

The page (2 July 1986) does the following.
(1) Each non-empty flag T={t_1<...<t_n} determines a figure F_T = {strata subordinate to T} = {P_{t_1},...,P_{t_n}, S_{t_1,t_2},...,S_{t_{n-1},t_n}}. This is the closed 'interval' [t_1,t_n] stratified by the points of T. It is drawn as a subdivided segment; points of L not in any [t_i,t_{i+1}] are 'forgotten'.
(2) Degenerate cases: T=∅ gives F=∅; T={t} gives {P_t}; T={a,b} gives the closed segment {S_{a,b},P_a,P_b}.
(3) A marginal NB adds that F_T determines T, via T=δF_T.
(4) On the set Drap*(L) of non-empty flags he puts the strict order T<T' ⇔ every t∈T is less than every t'∈T' (i.e. max T < min T'). This lets one speak of flags of flags, Drap*(Drap*(L)).
(5) A margin note: T<T' implies T∩T'=∅ and T∪T' ∈ Drap(L).
(6) Lemma: for T,T' ∈ Drap*(L), F_T and F_T' are compatible, equivalently geometrically disjoint (|o|), iff T and T' are comparable in Drap*(L). That is, {T,T'} is a flag of Drap*(L).

The next page draws the consequences. It deduces Drap(Drap*(L)) ≅ Fig_fin(M) via 𝒯 ↦ ⋃F_T, recovering the F_T as the connected components.

Purpose: a purely combinatorial description of 'tame' finite figures (finite unions of points and closed segments with their natural stratification) on an ordered line. This is a step in the 'Analysis situs' programme, building a combinatorial/tame topology from ordered sets.
errors: The 'i.e.' in the Lemma fails for T=T': {T,T}={T} is a flag of Drap*(L), yet F_T is not disjoint from itself. The intended condition is 'T≠T' and T, T' comparable' (T<T' or T'<T).

'Disjoint' (|o|) must be understood geometrically (closures/supports), not set-theoretically in M. For example, T={1,3} and T'={2} give F_T ∩ F_T' = ∅ as subsets of M, but S_{1,3} contains the point 2. Read this way the lemma is correct.

ideas.what: Canonical figure F_T attached to a finite subset T of a totally ordered set: a stratified closed interval, with T recoverable as δF_T
ideas.modern_name: Stratification of an interval by a finite set of points / cell decomposition of the line (o-minimal style)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard; o-minimal cell decomposition (van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn, 1980s)
ideas.where_published: Only the general 'tame topology' programme appears, in Esquisse d'un programme §5.

ideas.what: Order on non-empty finite subsets: T<T' iff max T < min T'; flags of flags
ideas.modern_name: Interval order on finite subsets / ordered set compositions

ideas.what: Disjointness of figures ⇔ comparability of flags, leading to finite figures ≅ Drap(Drap*(L))
ideas.modern_name: Classification of finite unions of closed intervals/points in a linear order (definable sets in dimension 1)

deep.surprise_reason: This is elementary and correct combinatorics of finite stratified subsets of an ordered line. It is of interest only as a documentation of how Grothendieck set up a combinatorial tame topology in 1986. Nothing here is new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely reads 'Déterminons maintenant toutes les figures. Tout drapeau T (non vide) de L détermine une figure F_T'. The struck fragment 'dans vide j. de L' is probably 'non vide de L'.
'X subordonné[?] par T' is plausibly 'X subordonné à T' or 'X subdivisé par T'; the meaning is the strata cut out by T.
In the T={a,b} line the hat notation denotes the closed segment, written \widetilde{S_{a,b}} on the neighbouring page.
The margin should read: 'NB T<T' ⇒ T||T' dans Drap*(L), T∪T' ∈ Drap(L). Comme on le voit dès l'énoncé, il est clair que T∩T'=∅'.
'avec [?] ...' before the a–b–c diagram is probably 'avec trois points' / 'puis si n=3'; this is uncertain.
